headline: Dry pre-Thanksgiving travel and a dry, mild holiday weekend around Mammoth Lakes and the Sierra, with gusty ridge-top winds Tuesday night and a possible return of winter storms on the passes as soon as Sunday night or Monday.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Patchy freezing fog in some eastern California valleys fades by late Tuesday morning. A weakening Pacific storm brings ridge-top wind gusts of 50–70 mph from late Tuesday morning through early Wednesday morning, but it falls apart as it reaches the Sierra, so the chance of any measurable rain or snow from I-80 south, including Mammoth Lakes, is below 10 percent. In northeast California and far northwest Nevada, a few light rain and snow showers are possible late Tuesday night into early Wednesday, with only a 20 percent or less chance of more than a trace.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: The storm's leftovers exit east Wednesday, leaving dry conditions for the busy travel period leading into Thanksgiving. From Thanksgiving through Friday, building high pressure brings warmer weather with highs in the 50s in most areas; cold air trapped in the valleys means Sierra communities and lower valleys see similar highs, while some spots above that cold layer could top 60 degrees. Freezing fog is likely in Truckee on Thursday and Friday mornings, and haze may build up around Reno those mornings.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Saturday stays dry and mild, and winds ahead of the next Pacific storm could push more valley spots to 60 degrees or higher, with only a low (up to 20 percent) chance of light showers near the Oregon border around Friday night. The next storm could bring winter conditions to the main Sierra passes as soon as Sunday, though it is trending weaker and a bit later, more likely Sunday night or Monday, so holiday travelers should keep winter gear handy. The overall trend favors a stronger storm by the start of December and an active, stormy pattern through the first week of the month.

watch_for: Timing of the late-weekend storm, which could bring winter driving conditions to the Sierra passes as soon as Sunday night or Monday.
Ridge-top wind gusts of 50–70 mph late Tuesday morning through early Wednesday.
A stronger storm and more active pattern possible in the first week of December.
confidence: Forecasters are confident in dry travel weather through Wednesday and a dry, mild Thanksgiving through Saturday, but uncertain about the timing and strength of the late-weekend storm and the stormier pattern into early December.
